Let the digits be assigned randomly to the positions A, B, C, D, E, F.

M·N = (100A + 10B + C)(100D + 10E + F), which expands into terms of the form (place value of M)(place value of N)·(digit in one position)(digit in the other).

Because the digits are drawn without replacement, for any two distinct positions the expected product of their digits is E[XY] = ((Σd)² − Σd²)/(6·5).

Here Σd = 21 and Σd² = 91, so E[XY] = (441 − 91)/30 = 350/30 = 35/3.

The sum of the place-value products is (100+10+1)(100+10+1) = 111² = 12321. Every pair (one position from M, one from N) involves two distinct positions, so each has the same expectation.

E[MN] = 12321 · 35/3 = 4107 · 35 = 143745.

ANSWER: 143745
